bug_semantics: Flask-Security-Too 5.8.0 OAuth reauthentication (verify) treats any datastore-resolved OAuth user as proof that the current session may be marked fresh. oauth_verify_response() calls _oauth_response_common(), then on a truthy user writes session['fs_paa']=time.time() with no check that that user is current_user. An attacker who already holds a stale authenticated victim session can start OAuth verify and complete the provider callback with a different account (attacker@example.com). The session identity stays the victim, but freshness is reset, so freshness-gated account actions (reproduced on built-in /change-username) succeed. oauthresponse() login is out of scope: it logs in as the OAuth user rather than minting freshness for a different session principal.
flaw_origin: The verify surface was first written in the single PR #1183 member 51a02457447387ca213f7b6c5fe90f158ebd3c6e (identical tree later squash-landed on main as 82575494312957332f9361cb8711af04d44a7a09). That commit added oauth_verify_start/oauth_verify_response and the unguarded if user: session['fs_paa']=time.time() path. Immediate parent 0c152879e2f877d9d00d4dfb88ab3dd73c68ab19 had OAuth login only (oauthresponse) and no fs_paa update. The 5.8.1 patch 8e69f3a94a463c0e8ddc46e31743717559fd8d48 changes the gate to if user and user.email == current_user.email.
